record.paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
record.context_brief: Bounded branch-width when large uniform minors are excluded
record.original_question: For every integer k, does there exist an integer n such that every excluded minor M for the class of real-representable matroids that has no U_{k,2k}-minor must have branch-width at most n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3. For every integer k there is an integer n such that, if M is an excluded minor for the class of R-representable matroids and M has no Uk,2k-minor, then M has branch-width at most n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $U_{r,n}$ denote the uniform matroid of rank $r$ on $n$ elements. A matroid $M$ is real-representable if there exists a matrix over $\mathbb{R}$ whose columns, with the linear-dependence structure inherited from $\mathbb{R}$, realize $M$. An excluded minor for the class of real-representable matroids is a matroid $M$ that is not real-representable, but every proper minor of $M$ is real-representable. The branch-width of a matroid $M$ on ground set $E$ is defined via branch-decompositions: a branch-decomposition of $M$ is a tree $T$ in which every internal vertex has degree $3$ and whose leaves are labeled bijectively by the elements of $E$; the width of an edge $e$ of $T$ is $r_M(A) + r_M(E\setminus A) - r(M) + 1$, where $A,E\setminus A$ is the partition of $E$ induced by removing $e$ from $T$, and the width of the decomposition is the maximum width over its edges; the branch-width of $M$ is the minimum width over all branch-decompositions of $M$ (with the convention that matroids with $|E| \le 1$ have branch-width $1$).

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $k$ there exists an integer $n = n(k)$ such that every excluded minor $M$ for the class of real-representable matroids which has no $U_{k,2k}$-minor satisfies $\mathrm{bw}(M) \le n$.
artifact.category_tag: matroid theory: excluded minors and branch-width
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is posed as a conjecture in the literature on excluded minors for real-representable matroids. Searches reveal no resolution: related work focuses on excluded minors for branch-width $k$ itself and for matroids representable over partial fields, but no proof or disproof of the stated conjecture about bounded branch-width of excluded minors with no $U_{k,2k}$-minor has been found.

status_evidence.snippet: Geelen, Gerards, Robertson, Whittle on bounding excluded minors for branch-width k.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not resolve the conjecture about real-representable excluded minors avoiding U_{k,2k}.

status_evidence.title: Computing excluded minors for classes of matroids representable over partial fields
status_evidence.snippet: Computational/structural approach to excluded minors for representability classes.
status_evidence.claim: No proof of the U_{k,2k} branch-width conjecture for R-representable matroids found.
